question: The Benasque-Cerler cable car, funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility, is subject to the ‘do no significant harm’ principle, as confirmed by the Commission in its reply to question E-004091/2025.

Subsequently, a court annulled the municipal agreements that had definitively approved the project on three grounds: the location of the departure station, ancillary buildings and a car park in a flood-prone area; the inadequacy of the geotechnical study of the route; and the absence of an economic feasibility study. Despite this, work continued.

Organisations defending the land and the environment have reported breaches of environmental regulations and a failure to provide compensation for the damage caused. Furthermore, the operation will depend on a subsidy from the Government of Aragón of around EUR two million per year to cover the projected deficit. In May 2026, I requested a meeting with the Commission to discuss this matter.
This request was reiterated in July but remained unanswered. In view of this situation: 1.
Has the Commission requested information from the Spanish authorities regarding these circumstances?
Does the Commission intend to verify compliance with environmental regulations and economic viability before considering the project to have been properly implemented?
If the breaches are confirmed, will the Commission take measures to protect the Union’s financial interests, including the recovery of funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.11.2026) Under Article 5(2) of Regulation (EU) 2021/2411, measures included in a Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) need to comply with the ‘Do No Significant Harm’ (DNSH) principle. The measure C14.

I1 ‘Transformation of the tourism model towards sustainability’ of the Spanish RRP2 imposes an obligation to comply with a list of excluded activities and the relevant EU and national environmental legislation.

This requirement was assessed positively under targets 217, 218 and 219 since it is included in the eligibility criteria of the calls for projects which had to be published under the Spanish Territorial Plans for Tourism Sustainability at Destinations. It is the responsibility of the Spanish authorities to ensure that these requirements are complied with during the implementation phase.

The Commission therefore encourages the Honourable Member to reach out to the Spanish authorities to enquire how they are monitoring the implementation of the DNSH conditions for this specific project.

Under this measure, milestone 221 ‘Actions related to tourism sustainability’ is currently being assessed by the Commission as part of Spain’s seventh payment request, which was submitted by the Spanish authorities on 30 September 2026. The Commission cannot comment on this ongoing assessment.

Projects put forward for the fulfilment of relevant milestones and targets need to meet the legal requirements under the Recovery and Resilience Facility Regulation and should comply with overall EU and national law.
